title: ESA and CAS release SMILE spacecraft footage of auroral oval
excerpt: The robotic spacecraft captured a full auroral oval in ultraviolet light during a one-hour time-lapse in late July.
bodyHtml:
ESA and CAS announced on October 6, 2026, that the robotic SMILE spacecraft has captured imagery of a complete auroral oval. An auroral oval is a circle of light around a magnetic pole that is typically too large to be seen from the ground.

The footage, released by the agencies, shows the phenomenon in ultraviolet light. The time-lapse covers approximately one hour of activity recorded in late July. The spacecraft's camera view shifts as it orbits the Earth, causing distant stars on the sides of the frame to appear to move.

According to the release, the SMILE spacecraft is designed to observe how the Sun's wind interacts with the Earth's magnetosphere. This data is intended to help understand how to protect astronauts, spacecraft, and ground-based electrical grids from solar storms.
